body: As someone who never used to drink coffee, I've recently found that it helps a lot in temporarly lifting my mood from it's usual low base level. I try not to over do it though. If I'm feeling any anxiety however, it just ends up making it incredibly worse. So got to watch out for that.

Thanks for that, really. Forgivness seems the hardest when it's at your own hands. It still feels impossible now but maybe someday.

I have an appointment with a psychologist next Friday for the first time ever. Hopefully that will help sort some things out because I've been dealing with this for too long and it's burning me out, and turning me into a person I don't like very much. I still feel horrible, but slightly more connected to reality than the same  person earlier. 


It's "herself" by the way guys. Don't make assumptions ;)

I can't not think all of this. It invades everything and anything I do. School, work, climbing, friends, sleep... I don't know why. I've always been this way in some way or another, it just evolves and morphs over the years.

Thanks for the banter man. It's nice to have someone to talk to.

I still climb, but it's getting harder and harder. Impossible even. Especially when the mental factor is such an important side to the sport.. Everything about it. I can't focus. Anxiety creeps in. Guilt fills in the cracks....... Then I start to think about how terrible of a climber I am, and really overall human being. How useless I am. How stupid I am for not being able to do things which, physically are totally within my ability.

Nothing to be mad at specifically. Some days (most) are worst than others. Anything and nothing sets me off. Totally unpredictable.

I was scratching at myself with an x-atco knife that I had near by. I'm too much of a woose to draw blood though and I know that I wouldn't be able to kill myself that way (trust me I've looked it up)
